title: WHO Declares PHEIC for Bundibugyo Ebola — Without Emergency Committee
detail: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus declared the Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) in DRC and Uganda a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), marking the 8th PHEIC declaration under modern IHR and the first ever issued without prior consultation with an Emergency Committee. The Director-General cited the high positivity rate of initial samples, confirmation of imported cases in Kampala, escalating suspected case trends, and ongoing armed conflict in Ituri as compounding the risk. As of 16 May, 8 laboratory-confirmed cases, 246 suspected cases, and 80 suspected deaths had been reported in Ituri Province, DRC. The DG subsequently convened the IHR Emergency Committee for May 19.

title: First American Tests Positive for Bundibugyo Virus in DRC, Evacuated to Germany
detail: Dr. Peter Stafford, an American medical missionary physician at Nyankunde Hospital in Bunia, DRC, tested positive for Bundibugyo ebolavirus disease on 17 May 2026. Stafford, who had been working in northeastern DRC since 2023, was exposed while caring for infected patients. He was medically evacuated to Germany for treatment and care. His wife, another doctor at the same charity, and four children — all asymptomatic — were also transferred to Germany for observation. CDC confirmed the case and stated that the risk to the US public 'remains low.' This was the first American citizen infected in the 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak.
